newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says N.Korean defector won't harm peace talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says N.Korean defector won't harm peace talks.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it saw no likelihood that an attempt by a senior North Korean official to defect to South Korea would affect planned talks on the future of the Korean peninsula.
Hwang Jang-yop, a leading North Korean ideologue, took refuge this week in the South Korean embassy in Beijing, sparking a diplomatic crisis between the two Koreas and China.

"We don't believe that this particular incident in Beijing is going to have an effect on the issues that are of primary concern to us ... including the agreed framework and the four-party talks," a State Department spokesman said.

Washington and Seoul have been trying to arrange a joint briefing for North Korean officials on a proposal for talks between the two Koreas, the United States and China on ending the state of war that technically still exists in Korea.
The United States is also concerned with maintaining a 1994 "agreed framework" that halts North Korea's existing nuclear programme in return for supply of modern nuclear power plants.

Pyongyang has already twice postponed the briefing, which is supposed to be held in New York, because of its failure so far to negotiate a grain import deal with U.S. trader Cargill Inc. to help alleviate famine in North Korea.
State Department Nicholas Burns said U.S. and North Korean officials met on Thursday in New York, but he gave no indication of any progress on the briefing.

Burns said that although the case of the defector was "of enormous interest to us," the United States had made no attempt to get involved and regarded it as a matter for South Korea and China to resolve.
